FILE ACCESS: your declared outputs are readable. Train 9 tin 1 defect found by a live test: the new board reuse probe cannot see the real launchd board. `boardAnswers` in tools/watch-cli.mjs requests `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/board?t=<token>`; the watch server refuses a query token on non-page API routes with 403 (it accepts the token only in the `x-watch-token` header or the strict cookie). So findRunningBoard returned null and `swarm watch --all` still started a second board (52001) next to the launchd board on 51058.

Fix:
- In tools/watch-cli.mjs `boardAnswers(url, fetchImpl)`: extract the token from the URL query, request `${u.origin}/api/board` with NO token in the URL, passing `headers: token ? { 'x-watch-token': token } : {}`, keeping redirect:'manual' and the 2 s timeout. Keep the success shape check (projects array + machine). Do not log the token; do not change the returned human URL format.
- Update tests/one-board-owner.test.mjs: in the watch-reuse test, make the fetch stub assert the request URL is exactly `${origin}/api/board` with no `t=` and that the `x-watch-token` header equals the identity token; return the board shape only under those conditions. Add a test that a board answering only without the header (or with a query token) is treated as not running and starts one board. Keep the existing stale/board.json tests green.

Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/one-board-owner.test.mjs tests/watch-token-urls.test.mjs tests/memory-fixes.test.mjs -> all pass. Do not start a real board; use stubs/temp dirs.
